title: Crushing the Serpent Under the Heel
narrative: The four missing Salvadorans are still missing, and the burned car found at Santo remains the only hard trace. What moved on 5 Nov was diplomacy and road traffic. In Madrid, Vice President Félix Ulloa told the Ibero-American Summit the Salvadoran troops are "not an occupation force" but a bilateral arrangement with Haiti, meant to bring the four home alive and help crush the gangs; he asked Latin America for solidarity and said joint work had already freed people held in a church and helped Chadian troops under fire. Haiti's Raina Forbin met him the same day. Her foreign ministry spoke only of strengthening the partnership; earlier in the week she had heard the same from El Salvador's foreign minister on the sidelines of the same summit.

On the ground, Haitian army trucks and Salvadoran armor left the Port-au-Prince airport at Clercine toward Croix-des-Bouquets or Tabarre. Haiti Defense Observer posted the video and said joint sightings of the two armies are becoming more common; Rolfy Martínez posted another and said the moves toward Tabarre bases go on while the fighting continues. He also posted Kenscoff residents going back to work without gang tolls after a joint push, and a thinner claim that wounded gang members crossed into the Dominican Republic on Monday after civilians tipped off the authorities.

A Haitian rights group, Fondasyon Je Klere, used Lanmò San Jou's letter to the UN as the occasion for a different ask: put Haiti–El Salvador cooperation under a clear UN-backed legal frame, break the contract with foreign private contractors (FJKL's own word is "mercenaires"), and spend that money training Haitian soldiers with Salvadoran help. It says nearly two years of the private deal freed no major road the firm had promised in six months, and it calls Viv Ansanm a terrorist group. Vectus itself still says nothing; Erik Prince's recent posts are about US politics, and the company site still does not mention Haiti. Cartel Watch had no Haiti item today.

Jake Johnston warns that disinformation about Haiti has risen since Bukele's intervention and reminds readers there is no peacekeeping mission there. Al Jazeera's 5 Nov wrap mostly retells the helicopter fighting, the burned vehicle and the UN's line that only about 200 Salvadorans sit under the Gang Suppression Force. The four are still nowhere to be found.

feed.who: Haiti Defense Observer (@HT_DefenseObsvr), Haitian defense watcher; also Rolfy Martínez (@RolfyMartinez)
feed.where: X, Clercine (near Port-au-Prince airport), heading toward Croix-des-Bouquets or Tabarre
feed.text: Posts a video (5 Nov) of Haitian army (FAd'H) armored trucks carrying Salvadoran troops, and Salvadoran armored vehicles, leaving the Port-au-Prince airport toward Croix-des-Bouquets or Tabarre. It says joint sightings of the two armies are becoming more common. Rolfy Martínez posted a similar video the same night, saying Haitian soldiers are still moving large numbers of Salvadorans and armored trucks toward bases in Tabarre and that they are still fighting the gangs.

feed.who: Félix Ulloa, vice president of El Salvador; Infobae (Elizabeth Minero); Centre à la Une (@Centrealaune); Diario El Salvador; EFE via Infobae agencies
feed.text: Speaking for Bukele on 5 Nov, Ulloa told the summit the Salvadoran troops in Haiti "are not an occupation force" and "not a unilateral decision," but "a bilateral arrangement with the Haitian authorities." He said the aim is to recover the four aviation technicians alive and help crush the gangs, appealed for Latin American solidarity with Haiti, and said joint operations have already freed people held in a church and helped a Chadian force under attack. Centre à la Une carries the same line in Creole. Diario El Salvador and the Haitian foreign ministry (via Infobae, evening of 5 Nov) say Raina Forbin also met Ulloa in Madrid that day to strengthen the security partnership; the ministry note gives no concrete new commitments.
feed.evidence: Quoted remarks at the summit (Infobae, EFE pool photos); Haitian foreign ministry photo and communiqué for the Forbin meeting
feed.other: Another source says (Juno7 / Haitian MFA, 3 Nov meeting with Hill Tinoco) El Salvador will stay as long as Haiti wants, inside the Gang Suppression Force and bilaterally. Ulloa's "church" rescue is not dated in the Infobae piece; Haitian outlets earlier reported 22 Full Gospel hostages freed in Arcahaie on 2 Nov by the police.

feed.who: Fondasyon Je Klere (FJKL); RHINEWS; Journal L'Observatoire; Zantray News; Centre à la Une (@Centrealaune)
feed.where: Port-au-Prince; report dated 4 Nov, carried 5 Nov
feed.text: In a 4 Nov report, FJKL asks the UN secretary-general to strengthen a Haiti–El Salvador military, security and judicial framework so the gangs lose what it calls "official impunity," and asks the Security Council's Counter-Terrorism Committee to help set the legal terms (status of the troops, duration, training of Haitian soldiers, trials). It also asks the Haitian government to break its contract with foreign private contractors — FJKL's own word in French is "mercenaires" — and put that money into mass training of Haitian soldiers with Salvadoran help. It says about 22 months of the private contract freed no major road the firm had promised within six months, calls Viv Ansanm a "terrorist group," and reads Lanmò San Jou's letter to Guterres as a bid for legitimacy, not a reason to talk. L'Observatoire and Zantray carry the same points; Centre à la Une summarizes them in Creole.
feed.evidence: FJKL report of 4 Nov, as quoted by RHINEWS, L'Observatoire, Zantray and Centre à la Une; we have not seen the full PDF
feed.other: Not yet reported by English-language wire services in this run. FJKL's "mercenaires" is the foundation's word, not ours.

feed.text: Posts a video he says shows Kenscoff residents going back to work freely after a joint operation by "united forces," the Haitian police and El Salvador, and says they can go to the city without fear of gang tolls or extortion.
feed.evidence: Video on his X account; no named on-camera witness; no status permalink recovered in this run (X posts endpoint returned 503)
feed.other: Not yet reported by others in those terms. Another source says (Le Midi Info, 3 Nov; Radio Télé Confiance) the army is consolidating Kenscoff and residents have gathered at the commissariat to support the new police chief; the town hall had earlier said returns would wait on sector-by-sector notice.

feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: A 5 Nov wrap repeats Bukele's patrol and helicopter videos, the burned vehicle find, Dujarric's line that only about 200 Salvadorans fall under the Gang Suppression Force, Fils-Aimé's assurance that foreign forces support the Haitian state, Lanmò San Jou's request for UN talks, the election delay to 18 Jul 2027, and an MSF warning from late October that 30 people wounded by gunfire and drone blasts were treated between 18 and 26 Oct.

feed.other: Another source says (MSF press release, 28 Oct) the same 30 wounded figure; the election delay was already on the page. Little new beyond packaging.

"We have no figures for that."

feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.where: X; Madrid, on the sidelines of the 30th Ibero-American Summit
feed.text: Foreign Minister Raina Forbin met French minister Éléonore Caroit, who it says pledged support for the Haitian police and army through training, equipment and building up their institutions. Le Nouvelliste reports that on Tuesday 3 Nov in Madrid Forbin also met Salvadoran Foreign Minister Alexandra Hill Tinoco, who said El Salvador will keep up its support for Haiti, "notamment au sein de la Force de Répression des Gangs (FRG)," despite the attack on four members of its contingent. They also discussed sharing experience against organized crime, protecting children from gangs, and disarmament and reintegration programs.
feed.evidence: Account report with photo; Le Nouvelliste article with photo of the two ministers
links: Le Nouvelliste, Forbin and Hill Tinoco

feed.text: Video of the mayor of Dajabón who, Martínez says, predicted a few days ago that the Salvadoran forces would fall to the Haitian gangs and now takes back what he said about Bukele and El Salvador.
feed.evidence: Video; the mayor is not named in the post
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Zanmi Lasante, the Haitian partner of Partners In Health, says in a note dated 4 Nov that its site at Santo was damaged because of the insecurity there. It does not describe the damage, but says the facilities affected play a big role in its work, so its medical resources are now affected, and asks that its facilities be protected.
feed.evidence: Organization's note, as reported; no photos of damage; no one named
feed.other: Le Nouvelliste also reported the note.

feed.evidence: Photo; no source named
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Edwin Paraison, a former Haitian consul in the Dominican Republic, says the four Salvadoran technicians may be dead, pointing to "various international sources and reports," and stresses they were doing technical work, not combat. He urges Bukele to redefine the goals of the Salvadoran military presence and to consider formally joining the Gang Suppression Force, and asks for an official report on the Salvadorans in Haiti.

feed.evidence: Police video; no names
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Salvadoran soldiers on foot patrol at Carrefour Rita at 13:00 local time on 4 Nov, with two helicopters overhead, in the area where the four Salvadorans were taken. Parrain Infos saw soldiers patrolling Tabarre at about 16:00 and says their destination and purpose are unknown. Haiti Defense Observer, citing Medya Laria, shows them on foot in Clercine, near the airport and the army's Clercine base, with helicopters overhead. Magazine Haïti and En Pak News also report patrols in Tabarre.

feed.who: Cartel Watch (@CartelWatchNet), US-based cartel news account
feed.text: Video it says shows a helicopter on patrol over Croix-des-Missions opening fire, with gunshots and flashes in the night sky, which it calls one of the first air operations by Salvadoran forces against the gangs.
feed.evidence: Night video; no time or source given
feed.other: Not yet reported by others as a separate event; it may be the same 3 Nov night firing that Infos Partage, Rolfy Martínez and Visegrád 24 posted.

feed.text: Analysis: the Arcahaie attacks of 31 Oct to 2 Nov, which it attributes to the Viv Ansanm coalition, were revenge for the 29 Oct police operation at Bercy in which, the mayor says, the gang leader "Galaxy" was killed. It says available evidence shows men driven out of Kenscoff joined the gangs in Arcahaie, and that attacking poorly protected villagers lets the gangs look strong as the police retake ground. It asks what the authorities planned to protect residents after the Bercy strike, since less than 48 hours passed before the reprisals.
feed.evidence: Analysis citing the mayor; the Kenscoff link is not sourced

feed.who: Radio Télé Confiance (@RTConfiance); Haitian National Police (@pnh_officiel)
feed.text: While operations go on in the Cul-de-Sac plain with the Gang Suppression Force, the Task Force and the Salvadoran force, the Haitian army is carrying on "consolidation" operations in Kenscoff, with soldiers still in the field to hold ground taken from the gangs. At 23:09 the police posted photos of an inspection and consolidation visit to Kenscoff by its western department chief (DDO-1).
feed.evidence: Radio report with photo, sources not named; police photos

feed.text: Says a 2 Nov memorial Mass in Croix-des-Missions, an area held by armed groups where schools and businesses have long been shut, was interrupted by gunfire; the priest had to stop and take cover.
feed.evidence: Video; no one named
feed.other: Rolfy Martínez also posted it (18:19).

feed.text: Video he says shows the fighting at Arcahaie, "where the united forces with El Salvador" fought the gangs.
feed.evidence: Video; place and time not shown in the clip
feed.other: Not yet reported by others. Another source says: the Arcahaie mayor credits the police and local self-defense brigades, and does not mention Salvadorans (Le Nouvelliste, Vant Bèf Info).

feed.who: Le Quotidien 509 (@lequotidien509E), Haitian news site, English account
feed.text: The police say they found the burned vehicle in which the four missing Salvadoran technicians were traveling, at Santo, during a joint operation with the Gang Suppression Force and Salvadoran soldiers. The police communiqué (via EFE in La Prensa Gráfica, and Proceso) says the operation began at about 6:30, used the UDMO, BRI, UTAG, SWAT, the Task Force and the drone team plus a barricade-clearing unit, met no resistance except one barricade, and that drone watch let it go off without incident. It says nothing about the fate of the four or about anything found inside the vehicle. Corvington Matin says Salvadoran soldiers were the ones who reached the area; AlterPresse: "still nowhere to be found."
feed.evidence: Police communiqué with photos of the burned vehicle; no one named
feed.other: Another source says the vehicle was found on Monday 2 Nov (El Diario de Hoy, Média Libre); agency copy on Proceso says the operation began on Tuesday.

feed.who: Infos Partage (@infospartagesos), Haitian news account; Corvington Matin
feed.text: The national brewery, BRANA, told its staff in an internal note that it is suspending work for now because of the security situation; a small team will keep up essential tasks, and a return to normal depends on events. Corvington Matin's editorial (18:53) says more private firms are closing while the prime minister spends more than $50 million a year on a private security company "with no result," and claims $24 million paid out for police equipment bought nothing.
feed.evidence: Photo of the internal note; editorial claims not sourced
feed.other: Parrain Infos also reported the closure (5 Nov, 03:48).

feed.text: DEBLOKE, the platform of former president Michel Martelly, says in a note of 3 Nov that it is false that Martelly asked the UN to suspend the Salvadoran operations, as the RHAJAC group had said. It says it backs Salvadoran support that respects Haiti's sovereignty and human rights. Juno7 notes the alleged request cannot be independently established.
feed.evidence: Political platform's written note
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Mayor Wilner René puts the toll of three days of gang attacks on Arcahaie, 31 Oct to 2 Nov, at 16 dead, among them civilians and members of self-defense brigades, with about ten wounded in the hospital. Some bodies were already decomposing and were buried quickly in a mass grave; people are missing, and 26 houses were burned and about 200 looted (Magazine Haïti summary).
feed.evidence: Named mayor, on the record
feed.other: Another source says: 43 dead (town officials via Rezo Nodwes, 2 Nov); see Numbers.

feed.text: In Creole: "The police, the force and the Salvadoran soldiers are mobilized to find the 4 Salvadoran technicians who disappeared in Santo."
feed.evidence: Police photo; no names

feed.text: "Police and force operation in Laplèn." Video.
feed.evidence: Police video; no names

feed.text: "Gangs were attacking GSF soldiers from Chad. We arrived quickly and repelled the attackers with our attack helicopters. The gangs no longer have the upper hand." It is the first time he has described his helicopters in combat; on 1 Nov he said they had not flown a single mission. Another source says the words come from a Gang Suppression Force report (EFE via El Nuevo Diario), though @GSForceHaiti has posted nothing on X since 1 Nov. feed.text: Lt. Gen. Derby Guerrier, head of the Haitian army, is in Benin from 3 to 7 Nov to work on officer training. Benin's army chief called Haiti "l'autre Bénin" ("the other Benin").
feed.evidence: Photos of the visit; named officers

feed.text: Mocked the 400 Mawozo leader's request for UN mediation in a "bingo card" post linking to AP. Magazine Haïti (03:59, 4 Nov) quotes him in French: "And if the gang leaders stopped attacking international forces, terrorizing the police and abusing the Haitian people, maybe then we could talk about mediation."

feed.where: X and web, UN noon briefing in New York
feed.text: UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said the letter from 400 Mawozo came by email; about 200 Salvadorans are under the Gang Suppression Force and the rest are "a bilateral issue"; "respond is a pretty big and vast word." The Miami Herald ("Who do Salvadoran troops answer to if they aren't part of the UN force in Haiti?") adds that the Salvadorans skipped UN human rights training, that no signed agreement is public, that the prime minister's office oversees the Vectus Global drone task force, and that the 2 Nov Cul-de-Sac operation barely came under fire as gangs fall back (one source). Another source says the UN refused the dialogue outright (Radio Télé Confiance, 22:47).
feed.evidence: On-camera briefing; Herald article with named officials and one unnamed source

feed.who: Office of the Prime Minister (@PrimatureHT); also Magazine Haïti, Centre à la Une, Diario El Mundo, Haiti Defense Observer
feed.where: X and web, Villa d'Accueil, Port-au-Prince
feed.text: At a security press conference, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé said the police, the army and the Gang Suppression Force, with El Salvador's help, now share one plan: "Our goal is clear: to end gang rule and restore state authority" (Diario El Mundo). He said the forces passed 4,000 with the Salvadoran arrivals (Centre à la Une), thanked Bukele, and said all forces act under Haitian command. In Creole: "gang yo pa p gen dòmi nan je" ("the gangs will get no sleep"), and both "gangs in sandals" and "gangs in ties" will face sanctions (Magazine Haïti, 19:48). Beside him stood Maj. Gen. Jonas Jean (army), Brig. Elon Clarke (Jamaica, Gang Suppression Force deputy commander), Col. José Roberto Figueroa (El Salvador) and police chief Vladimir Paraison (Haiti Defense Observer). The communiqué is titled "The state goes on the offensive against the gangs."
feed.evidence: Official communiqué with 4 photos; press conference on record

feed.who: Magazine Haïti (@maghaiti), citing Arcahaie interim mayor Wilner René on Radio Magik9
feed.text: The mayor said at least 22 kidnapped people were freed at Bercy on 2 Nov, others are still missing, and some people were burned inside houses the gangs set on fire; attacks have gone on since Galaxie and about 20 men were killed on 29 Oct. Radio Télé Confiance says the police and the self-defense brigades retook the road from Thomas to Bercy and freed about 22 Full Gospel church members held since 31 Oct, and gives about 20 gang members killed. Centre à la Une says suspected "Taliban" gang members were killed at Vigner and Pon Toman. Rolfy Martínez posted video of the Arcahaie checkpoint taken back by police and brigades (18:51).
feed.evidence: Named mayor on radio; video of checkpoint

feed.who: Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), Center for Economic and Policy Research
feed.text: "There is no peacekeeping mission in Haiti." At 17:35: "Truly a new level of disinfo and fake news on Haiti ever since a certain Central American leader started getting involved." Earlier (05:05) he pointed to the UN saying most Salvadorans are outside the Gang Suppression Force.
feed.evidence: Analyst's posts

feed.text: Chérizier said the FBI should investigate the gang leader "Ezekiel," who spread rumors of his own death and is said to be in Canada; HaitiInfoProj reads it as a sign Chérizier is cooperating with the FBI. Centre à la Une reported the same remarks at 19:44.
feed.evidence: Gang leader's own video statement (not linked); interpretation is the account's own

feed.who: Centre à la Une (@Centrealaune), Haitian news site
feed.text: Photo of a Viv Ansanm barricade across a road in Croix-des-Bouquets.
feed.evidence: Photo; photographer not named

feed.text: Sums up several informal polls on social media, including people who say they live in displacement camps: "overwhelming opposition to amnesty for gangs," and most see the government and police as too corrupt.
feed.evidence: Informal online polls; no figures or method given

feed.text: Asks how the prime minister could sign a contract of more than $50 million with a foreign firm, renew it a year later, and then say on Friday that the country's security cannot depend on foreign forces; it says the firm has produced no result in more than 17 months. The firm is not named; the figure matches the one other outlets give for the Vectus-linked drone task force.
feed.evidence: Opinion with no document

feed.text: Photo of "5 Segond" gang members from the Bercy base who had climbed the walls along a street in Arcahaie before police and residents drove them back; at 06:50 it said the gangs "never stopped attacking Arcahaie" and got reinforcements. Rolfy Martínez (06:02) posted video of Arcahaie residents celebrating the police win over Viv Ansanm; HaitiInfoProj (15:38) relayed a local note on the celebration.
feed.evidence: Photo and video; local residents not named

feed.text: "Press Blackout Imposed": according to several sources, journalists may not photograph or film Salvadoran patrols in Port-au-Prince, and some have had guns pointed at them.
feed.evidence: Several unnamed sources
feed.other: Matches the video of a Salvadoran soldier asking people not to film (Rolfy Martínez, 04:21).

feed.text: Says Prime Minister Fils-Aimé visited the Salvadoran base after the 2 Nov operation and that finding the four missing soldiers is still the mission's main goal.
feed.evidence: Video and photos of the visit

feed.text: Video of a Salvadoran soldier with the joint forces asking people "please" not to film and to delete the videos and pictures they have taken, while, in Martínez's words, the troops "keep cleaning the streets of Haiti."
feed.evidence: Video (about 4 minutes); the soldier is not named; place and date of filming not given
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.who: Gabriel Elizondo (@elizondogabriel), Al Jazeera at the UN
feed.text: Posts UN spokesman Dujarric's 2 Nov statement on the letter signed by Wilson Joseph (Lanmò San Jou) for "Gwoup Rebel 400": receiving it is not endorsing it, and the vast majority of Salvadoran troops are not under the Gang Suppression Force.
feed.evidence: UN statement text

feed.who: Planet News HT (@ht_planet) and @MackensonO35867, Haitian news accounts, citing Radio YSUCA 91.7 FM (San Salvador)
feed.where: X, Creole, citing a Salvadoran radio station
feed.text: Salvadoran radio YSUCA reports that the Salvadoran authorities have suspended leave for soldiers and police officers as they prepare to send a new security contingent to Haiti. The number of new troops and police has not been given.
feed.evidence: Named radio station; no document, no named official
feed.other: Not yet reported by others. A web search found no YSUCA page or other outlet carrying it.

feed.who: AP, reporter Dánica Coto (@danicacoto), interview with Wilson Joseph ("Lanmò San Jou"), leader of 400 Mawozo; summary by NAGO.TV
feed.where: AP (Washington Post copy) and NAGO.TV, Haiti
feed.text: The 400 Mawozo leader told AP on Monday that he did write to UN Secretary-General Guterres asking for a delegation to come to Haiti for dialogue and mediation; AP calls it his first interview with a major international news company. According to NAGO.TV's summary of the AP story, he says he is ready to lay down his weapons and sets terms for a peace commission, says Haitian politicians armed the gangs, denies killing innocent people and says drone strikes kill civilians. He told AP the four missing Salvadorans are dead and that the attack happened in Chen Mechan territory; he gave no evidence. The Haitian government says the four were abducted, and the Salvadoran government believes they are alive. AP says fighting has intensified in the Cul-de-Sac plain between armed men and the Gang Suppression Force, police, soldiers and Vectus Global. He has been under UN sanctions since 8 Dec 2023 and is under US indictment over the 2021 kidnapping of missionaries. Rezo Nodwes says the AP story backs what it reported on Sunday night.
feed.evidence: Named gang leader, interviewed by a named reporter (phone or in person not stated); no evidence for his claim about the four
feed.other: Another source says: a search summary of the AP story quotes UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric as saying the UN received a letter bearing his signature, and that receipt does not mean the UN endorses it or recognizes him; NAGO.TV says the UN had not responded publicly. The AP site itself was blocked to us.

feed.text: Posts a short video he says shows "the true face" of Lanmò San Jou, and says the 400 Mawozo leader has nearly 6,000 people in his criminal network and "lived quietly until President Bukele came to Haiti to look for his soldiers." Earlier (17:03 and 18:07 on 2 Nov) he posted the gang leader's Day of the Dead video in a suit and watches, and the video in which he asks for a general dialogue, rejects foreign intervention and vows to fight for his land.
feed.evidence: Video (23 seconds); the 6,000 figure has no source
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.
links: Day of the Dead video post

feed.who: Magazine Haïti (@maghaiti), Centre à la Une (@Centrealaune) and Amerique.info7 (@AmeriqueInfo7), Haitian news accounts
feed.where: X, Creole; Canaan and La Plaine (Plaine du Cul-de-Sac)
feed.text: Magazine Haïti says several thousand people marched in Canaan on Monday 2 Nov "under pressure from the gangs" against the Salvadoran soldiers, in white T-shirts, with placards and microphones, chanting "Down with invasion," "Stop shedding the people's blood in La Plaine" and "We will not move, we do not want violence, we want education." They called themselves members of the group Kanaran Debou. It says the police broke up the march. Amerique.info7 says Viv Ansanm forced residents of La Plaine into the streets under threat of death and that marchers sent warnings to Bukele. Centre à la Une says marchers from several Croix-des-Bouquets neighborhoods chanted "Down with invasion, we want peace, we will not move," and that, according to its sources, the gang leaders made them march to sway public opinion.
feed.evidence: Photos and video posted by the three accounts; marchers not named; sources for the threats not named
feed.other: EFE also says "some media" report that Viv Ansanm forced La Plaine residents to march under threat of death.

feed.who: @GwokzeGrandosye, Haitian account following the Moïse trial; Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), CEPR, replied "Yup"; Jacqueline Charles (@Jacquiecharles), Miami Herald; Magazine Haïti (@maghaiti)
feed.where: X, from the federal trial of Christian Emmanuel Sanon in Miami
feed.text: Former Colombian soldier Mario Antonio Palacios testified that a police officer at President Jovenel Moïse's residence told the attackers the main gate would be left open. The post points to a Haitian judicial police (DCPJ) report of 2 Aug 2021 (page 33), in which Naiser Franco Castañeda said Joseph Félix Badio told them the driver would leave the gate open, and to Jude Laurent, named as an insider; it says it "cannot yet establish" that Laurent is the officer. Jake Johnston replied "Yup." Jacqueline Charles, live from court, reports Palacios admitting he took Martine Moïse's two watches and a necklace and money from the house ("I made the mistake of taking them"), that the 21 soldiers were promised $2,600 a month and later a $300,000 bonus each, and "We were lied to, duped." Lawyer Gordon Phenil Désir, handed to the US by the Haitian police, made his first court appearance and said he cannot afford a private lawyer; Magazine Haïti, citing the Miami Herald, says he is accused of bringing the Colombians to Port-au-Prince and translating for them.
feed.evidence: Court testimony by a named witness; photos of the DCPJ report; reporter in the courtroom

feed.who: Nayib Bukele (@nayibbukele), president of El Salvador; video by @daphneydss, Haitian account
feed.where: X, Haiti (place of filming not given)
feed.text: Bukele quote-posted, with only a Salvadoran flag, a video posted at 23:33 by @daphneydss with the Creole caption "Men mesye Bukele yo atè a" ("Here are Bukele's men on the ground"), showing Salvadoran soldiers on foot and in armored vehicles. He also reposted EFE on the first big operation, a Bloomberg story headlined "Haiti Gang Leader Calls for Peace After El Salvador Sends Troops," DW and Dominican senator Vinicio Castillo (@VinicioSenador), who wrote that the troops are well armed and that if the gangs hand over their weapons it would be a "historic achievement." Salvadoran outlets (SoyANoticias, Alerta Noticias, Cronio, Su Mundo) present the video as Bukele showing the operation. He has made no new statement of his own.
feed.evidence: Video (about 3 minutes); place and date of filming not given

feed.who: Punto 503 (@Puntosv503), Salvadoran commentary account; another view from @Latinar_rybar
feed.text: A long video "analysis" says the Salvadoran troops have set up their base in Tabarre next to the US Embassy and are patrolling by land and air around Croix-des-Bouquets, calls the UNA-Haiti letter about bombings a "farce" by a "front" NGO, and says 400 Mawozo and Chen Mechan are boxed in in the Cul-de-Sac plain. "For the leaders of terror, the final destination is not a dialogue table: it is CECOT" (El Salvador's mega-prison).
feed.evidence: Video (about 31 minutes) of commentary; no named sources
feed.other: Another source says: @Latinar_rybar (20:35 on 2 Nov) calls the patrols videos "edited for social media," says the troops stay on paved roads near the embassy and airport and avoid the 400 Mawozo stronghold; it also names no sources.

feed.who: EFE, Spanish news agency (photos by Jonet St. Élois), carried by Diario Libre
feed.text: Salvadoran troops launched their first big operation on Monday 2 Nov in the Cul-de-Sac plain northeast of Port-au-Prince, aiming to break up Chen Mechan and 400 Mawozo, which are blamed for the disappearance of the four. About ten armored vehicles took part. A video shows the vehicles moving through areas that look abandoned while gang members put up barricades. Citing the Haitian press, EFE says at least ten gang members were killed at Santo and Croix-des-Missions. It quotes the police statement (see the police item) and notes the US reward of up to $1 million for Lanmò San Jou.
feed.evidence: Agency report; video circulating online; Haitian press and the police statement as sources

feed.who: Magazine Haïti (@maghaiti), Le Facteur Haïti (@LeFacteurHaiti) and Arcahaie residents on X
feed.where: X, Creole and French; Bèsi (Bercy), Arcahaie
feed.text: While the police hit La Plaine, Magazine Haïti says they are also fighting gangs at Bèsi in Arcahaie, where "more than 20 bandits" have fallen. Le Facteur Haïti says drones of the police and the Task Force struck at Croix-des-Bouquets and Arcahaie on Monday "in response to gang attacks." From Arcahaie, @douvanjouenfo wrote at 18:06 that the town had been under Viv Ansanm attack for about three days and that no reinforcements had arrived, "counting bodies" and burning houses; @OClaudette67756 wrote to the Gang Suppression Force at 20:07 "SOS for Arcahaie... day 4 of the battle," saying Viv Ansanm already holds a small part of the town. @daphneydss said a helicopter was striking Viv Ansanm over Arcahaie on Monday morning.
feed.evidence: Named outlets; residents' posts; one photo; no official toll
feed.other: Not yet reported by others (the Bèsi toll).

feed.who: Haitian Network of Anti-Corruption Journalists (RHAJAC), note of 2 Nov; reported by SkandalNews (@SkandalNews), Satellite 509 (@satellite509) and Rezo Nodwes
feed.text: RHAJAC says, "according to its information," that former president Michel Martelly asked Harvey Dupiton, Randolf St Leger and Jean Philippe Vixamar to send the 28 Oct UNA-Haiti letter to the UN denouncing bombings in Croix-des-Bouquets, Canaan and the Cul-de-Sac plain, in a bid to stop the Salvadoran operations. It links this to his political ambitions and speaks of promised amnesty for gang leaders in exchange for support. It asks Haitian judges and UN experts to investigate.
feed.evidence: Statement by a named press group; SkandalNews notes it gives no public evidence

feed.who: Haitian National Police (@pnh_officiel); statement relayed by Radio Métronome (@Radio_Metronome), Jacqueline Charles (Miami Herald) and Centre à la Une
feed.where: X, Creole and French; Plaine du Cul-de-Sac
feed.text: "The police are carrying out a big operation in La Plaine." The police statement says it launched the operation on Monday with the support of the Gang Suppression Force in several parts of the Cul-de-Sac plain, to destroy illegal toll barriers, stop kidnapping attempts and end gang violence against residents, and that armored vehicles sent by the high command are concentrated at Kafou Chada, the Croix-des-Missions bridge and Santo 17. Jacqueline Charles: "Haiti police with support of the @GSForceHaiti is currently launching an operation in Plain of the Cul-de-Sac." Centre à la Une notes the statement does not mention the Salvadorans.
feed.evidence: Official statement; photo

feed.text: Posts photos of former police officer Johnson André, leader of the Izo 5 Segond gang, and says "it is said" that his second in command was killed after exchanges with "the united forces" and the police in Village de Dieu. "They are starting to fall."
feed.evidence: Three photos; "it is said," no source named; the dead man is not named
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.who: Michael Paarlberg (@MPaarlberg), US political scientist who studies El Salvador; quoted by Haiti Information Project
feed.text: Calls the deployment "a publicity stunt with no clear military objective," meant to save face before Bukele's reelection bid, since it is not known whether the four aviation technicians are alive.
feed.evidence: Named analyst's opinion

feed.who: Amerique.info7 (@AmeriqueInfo7), PouSiOuPaTKonnen (Eddyson de Varain), Radio graphie, Radio Patriarche and others
feed.where: Haitian press, French and Creole; Santo, Croix-des-Missions and Chada, Croix-des-Bouquets
feed.text: Heavy fighting from midday on Monday, the Day of the Dead, at Santo and Croix-des-Missions, Chen Mechan's stronghold, between the police, backed by Salvadoran soldiers, and the gangs. PouSiOuPaTKonnen, citing "concordant sources," says kamikaze drones were used and about ten gang members were killed, according to unofficial reports. Radio graphie lists helicopters, exploding drones, armored vehicles and ground troops, gives "a dozen dead" among the gangs from its sources, says the police note names the units at Santo, Croix-des-Missions and Chada but gives no figures, and has video of an armored column heading toward the 400 Mawozo stronghold, with Salvadoran soldiers seen. Planet News HT says gangs blocked several roads with big rocks to slow the advance. Radio Patriarche: "This toll remains to be confirmed by the authorities."
feed.evidence: Video of the armored column; unnamed local sources for the toll
feed.other: Another source says: Planet News HT notes the Gang Suppression Force said on 1 Nov that it does not use explosive devices, including the Salvadoran contingent and its helicopters.

feed.text: Compares the 28 Oct UNA-Haiti letter (Harvey Dupiton) and the 1 Nov letter in Lanmò San Jou's name, both to Guterres: similar wording and timing on the eve of the US midterm elections. It says there is "no tangible proof of collusion" and sets out three scenarios for how the US vote could affect Haiti policy.
feed.evidence: Analysis of two documents; no named sources

feed.who: Deus Deronneth (@Deus_Deronneth), former deputy for Marigot and presidential hopeful
feed.text: Says he is deeply worried about the Salvadoran deployment and mission. The disappearance of the four puts Prime Minister Didier Fils-Aimé in difficulty, he says, and has brought Trump, Bukele and Dominican President Abinader closer on Haiti, each defending his own country's interests: "But who is defending Haiti's interests?" He asks the prime minister to explain the mission.
feed.evidence: Named politician's statement

feed.who: Diario Libre (@DiarioLibre), Dominican daily, citing the Dominican foreign ministry
feed.where: Diario Libre, Port of Haina, Dominican Republic
feed.text: A ship left the Port of Haina on Sunday 1 Nov for Haiti carrying about 525 tonnes of supplies, weapons, specialized vehicles and support equipment for the Gang Suppression Force. The cargo came from Bangladesh, and Germany paid to move it to the Dominican Republic. Daniela Kroslak, UN Assistant Secretary-General and head of the UN Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH), called Dominican logistical help "essential." Dominican vice ministers Rubén Silié and Ramón Pérez Fermín and German Ambassador Maike Friedrichsen attended. Listín Diario and El Diario de Hoy, citing the Dominican foreign ministry, quote Kroslak: the shipment "includes containers, vehicles and any other military equipment." El Diario de Hoy notes that the ministry did not say how many vehicles there are or which units will get them. Le Quotidien 509 adds that command structure and coordination for the force are still being worked out, and that Kroslak raised the need for housing, food and medical care for the troops.
feed.evidence: Named UN and Dominican officials, from a foreign ministry press release; photos of the ship
feed.other: Another source says: Diario Libre (1 Nov, 18:43) says the gear is for the Bangladeshi contingent of about 1,600 soldiers and police and was flown in from Germany, with armored vehicles in the video. Le Nouvelliste (30 Oct) and HaitiBoiii say more than 600 tonnes.
links: Diario Libre, gear for Bangladesh troops

feed.who: Alerta Noticias (@alertanoti), Salvadoran news account, and Diario El Mundo (San Salvador)
feed.where: X and Diario El Mundo, Tabarre
feed.text: Video of Salvadoran troops in armored vehicles and combat gear on patrol in Tabarre, where the contingent has set up its base. Diario El Mundo says the troops are on their third day of patrols, in Tabarre near Santo, in the Croix-des-Bouquets district where the four were ambushed, and that some passers-by applauded the convoy. It quotes Bukele (Thursday): "If we finished off the gangs here, we can finish them off. It is their decision [the Haitians'] whether they want us to finish them off or not."
feed.evidence: Video (72 seconds); named newspaper

feed.who: Serge Pierre Louis (@SERGEPLOUIS), head of the Haïti Solidaire party
feed.text: On the letter signed in the name of Lanmò San Jou: it is dated 1 Nov 2026 at Croix-des-Bouquets, asks Guterres for a UN delegation to mediate between "the international forces" and 400 Mawozo, and lists copies to the OAS and CARICOM. "The document alone does not allow us to confirm either its authenticity or its receipt by these institutions." He asks "who advises the gangs, prepares their arguments and seeks to open the doors of international recognition for them?" and wants the authorities to investigate the gangs' backers.
feed.evidence: Named politician; photo of the letter

feed.text: Fighting in several parts of Arcahaie (Vignier, Thoman, Bercy) is said to have left 43 dead, 13 of them civilians, and 18 wounded, according to a provisional toll that local media attribute to town officials. The police and national authorities have not given these figures. The fighting followed the killing of the gang leader "Galaxy" on 29 Oct at Bercy by the police and the Task Force. Many residents have left their homes, and Mayor Wilner René is asking for reinforcements. Rezo Nodwes says the risk to reporters in the area makes independent checking hard.
feed.evidence: Local toll from town officials, relayed by local media; no names; photo
feed.other: Another source says: Centre à la Une (02:58) says more than 30 people died, civilians among them, in fighting on Sunday 1 Nov at La Vigne and Pon Toman; Radio Métronome (1 Nov, 15:13) gave a partial toll of at least seven dead.

feed.where: X, in Creole, Spanish and English
feed.text: "First success of Bukele's intervention in Haiti: everyone who was supporting the gangs has been forced to show themselves. They are all insulting the President of El Salvador!" He thanks Bukele: "The Haitian people stand with you!" Earlier (00:26) the diaspora group Amid International posted: "UNA-Haiti does not speak for all Haitians... We are grateful to President Bukele and the Salvadoran people."
feed.evidence: Opinion posts by a named journalist and a named group; no evidence offered

feed.who: War Noir (@war_noir), weapons and conflict researcher
feed.text: Video of Haitian gang members celebrating Halloween in costume "during the clashes with UN-backed Forces and Salvadoran Forces." War Noir says at least one carries what may be a refurbished US-made M16A1 (Colt Model 603) pattern rifle, which it calls "rather common." Place and date of filming not given.
feed.evidence: Video (43 seconds); weapon read by a named researcher; place not given
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: A letter dated 1 Nov 2026 in the name of Wilson Joseph ("Lanmò San Jou"), under the heading "Bureau Communication" of 400 Mawozo, asks UN Secretary-General António Guterres to send a delegation to Haiti for mediation and a dialogue for peace. The signer says he raised a "white flag" on 20 Aug and is ready to talk with the international forces; he speaks of violence in the Cul-de-Sac plain, incidents involving Salvadoran soldiers and civilian victims, including an eight-year-old girl. The letter says "the weapon of dialectic must prevail over that of arms." Rezo Nodwes asks who wrote it, and links it to Pastor Malory Laurent's claim on Sunday that men close to power lean on gangs. Caleb de Ra Paul (02:55) says the letter denounces the Salvadoran operations in the plain.
feed.evidence: Photo of the letter; author not known
feed.other: Another source says: GJB NewsHT (02:13) adds that the letter says the eight-year-old was shot in the head.

feed.who: Rezo Nodwes (@rezo_nodwes), citing police union SPNH-17 coordinator Inspector Garry Jean-Baptiste
feed.text: The police union SPNH-17 says more than 60 percent of the Haitian National Police serves as bodyguards for officials and business figures, while the front against the gangs is short of men. Examples given: six officers for 150,000 people at Marchand-Dessalines before its station was destroyed, ten on La Gonâve. The prime minister's motorcade is "full" of officers from special units trained for urban combat.
feed.evidence: Named union official; former senior officers not named
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Video of Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé at the graduation of the 37th police class: "Experience shows us that the security of the country cannot depend on foreign forces." He promises to strengthen the police against the armed groups. Corvington Matin asks whether he is opposing the Salvadoran intervention or reminding Haitian institutions of their duty: "The timing of his statement is striking."
feed.evidence: Video (65 seconds) of the prime minister speaking

feed.text: Images circulating of the 400 Mawozo leader, Lanmò San Jou, in a field cutting trees, guarded by several armed men. "The leader is still at large and without fear." Place and date not given.
feed.evidence: Video (34 seconds); place and date not given
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Posts a YouTube interview in which Defense Minister Mario Andrésol answers Marche Longue's questions on the new doctrine of the Armed Forces of Haiti (FAd'H), the updated military code, modernization and the army's part in operations.
feed.evidence: Video interview with the named minister (link only; we did not watch it)

feed.who: Listín Diario (@ListinDiario), Dominican daily, interviewing Edwin Paraison, former Haitian consul in the Dominican Republic
feed.text: Paraison says Haitians back Bukele's decision and that "for the first time I have noticed that fear is beginning to take hold of them." He says the latest reports speak of men deserting the gang of Joseph Wilson (Lanmò San Jou) and that of Claudy Célestin (Chen Mechan). Some sectors worry that the Salvadorans answer to their own high command, not to the Gang Suppression Force. He fears the four are no longer alive, and says rumors in Haiti hold that they went to the place of the attack without protection.
feed.evidence: Named former official, interview; no evidence given for the desertions

feed.who: Jacqueline Charles (@Jacquiecharles), Miami Herald, and the US Embassy (@USEmbassyHaiti)
feed.text: American Airlines resumed daily Miami to Cap-Haïtien flights on 1 Nov (flight AA2492), with an all-Haitian, Creole-speaking crew; Haiti has had no regular service by a major airline since the late-2024 gang gunfire that led to the FAA ban on US carriers at Port-au-Prince, which "remains in effect." Haiti's consul general in Miami, Yverick Delerme Cyril, says the government is working on security so the capital's airport can reopen too. The US Embassy (00:11) "welcomes the return of American Airlines flights to Haiti," in Creole, French and English.
feed.evidence: Named reporter on the flight; named officials; photos and video

feed.text: The border provinces of Independencia and Pedernales keep up military watch, migration checks and intelligence work along the line with Haiti. Jimaní's Mal Paso crossing connects to the road to Port-au-Prince. The paper ties the stepped-up watch to the 18 Oct disappearance of the four Salvadorans.
feed.evidence: Named newspaper; no officials named

feed.who: Rolfy Martínez (@RolfyMartinez) and Caleb de Ra Paul (@calebderapaul), relaying Harvey (Hervé) Dupiton of UNA-Haiti
feed.text: In a video, Hervé Dupiton, head of the diaspora group UNA-Haiti, which wrote to the UN saying Salvadoran forces bombed civilians, says he woke up to many messages and photos attacking him after Bukele's denial. He says "he fights for Haiti and Bukele for El Salvador." Le Quotidien 509 (20:09), citing Diario Co Latino of San Salvador, says UNA-Haiti denounces the deaths of innocent civilians, including children.
feed.evidence: Video (60 seconds) of the named man speaking

feed.text: Video in which Wilson Joseph ("Lanmò San Jou"), named as the 400 Mawozo leader, asks to make peace with Bukele. He says he is not looking to start a war, is ready to talk, and denies that his group is involved in the case of the four missing technicians.
feed.evidence: Video (115 seconds) of the gang leader speaking

feed.who: Magazine Haïti (@maghaiti), citing the Haitian National Police (@pnh_officiel)
feed.text: The police say they are standing firm against the gangs in Arcahaie after the attack of Saturday 31 Oct, with the departmental operations brigade (BOID) and the crowd-control unit (CIMO). Residents kept sending SOS calls on Sunday 1 Nov. The police statement (via InnovaNews7, 16:44, and Radio Métronome) says the attackers were pushed back at Bési (Bercy) at about 2 a.m. on 31 Oct, two days after an operation that killed about 20 gang members, among them their leader "Galaxie," a position it says was held by the "Taliban" gang. The police posted a photo early on 1 Nov: "The police stand up to the terrorist bandits' attacks in Akayè."
feed.evidence: Police statement; police photo
feed.other: Another source says: Corvington Matin (19:29) quotes a tearful resident: "Between the police statement and the reality on the ground there is a gap... Our houses were burned," and says officers on site need reinforcements that are slow to come.

feed.text: "Barricades, forced recruitment, demonstrations under duress": the strongest gangs in the Port-au-Prince area are preparing for possible operations in the Cul-de-Sac plain as Bukele threatens to intervene. Trapped, some residents flee their neighborhoods while others are forced to take part in the gangs' preparations. (We could read only the headline and summary; the page loads its text by script.)
feed.evidence: Named outlet; sources inside the article not read

feed.text: "The situation is still complicated" in Arcahaie: each time the police and the brigade try to push the gangs back, they get more reinforcements. Residents renew their call for the central government to help. On Sunday morning (16:27 post, with video) it said the gangs were still advancing in the town while the brigade and police held out.
feed.evidence: Local reporting; video from the morning

feed.text: Haitian citizens gathered to ask Bukele to intervene in Haiti, saying both the gangs and "the corruption of the current government" keep Haiti from being free. Place not given. Girasol TV (2 Nov, 01:20) posts the same video.
feed.evidence: Video (486 seconds); speakers not named; place not given

feed.who: Eduardo Menoni (@eduardomenoni) and Caleb de Ra Paul (@calebderapaul)
feed.text: Video of Haitian residents handing bottles of water to Salvadoran soldiers and Haitian police during operations against the gangs. Menoni: "The people of Haiti are grateful to President Bukele." Caleb de Ra Paul (21:52) posts the same images in Creole as "a sign of gratitude." Place not given.
feed.evidence: Video (27 seconds); place not given

feed.who: Danny Shaw (@profdannyshaw), US professor and activist
feed.text: Shaw calls the operation an "invasion" that "goes far beyond the matter of the four kidnapped Salvadorans, who most likely are already dead," and "a question of total US domination." He says the empire has changed strategy: instead of paramilitary groups, "it now uses mercenaries as its force on the ground."
feed.evidence: Video (310 seconds) of a named commentator; no evidence offered

feed.text: Photos of Armed Forces of Haiti (FAd'H) troops and armored trucks carrying and escorting Salvadoran army personnel to their garrison in the Tabarre area. "It appears the Salvadoran troops will be working in a joint-force dynamic with the Haitian Army. No confirmation yet if any defense memorandums or accords are to be signed." Rolfy Martínez (18:43) posts video of the same convoy.
feed.evidence: Four photos; video

feed.text: "Several people have died in the area near the main cemetery in Port-au-Prince." A large house known as the Gabelis house "was destroyed by a drone, with several people inside"; a fried-food vendor and her husband died. Gangs are moving their dead from their camps, with "gang ambulances" picking up at least a dozen killed by gunfire, and are leaving Salomon toward Potay. "4 civilians and at least 13 gang members were killed last night." Earlier (12:02): gangs set houses on fire in Chandel late on 31 Oct, and at 2 a.m. there was heavy gunfire downtown "and use of drones."

feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: On National Road 8, Jimaní to Port-au-Prince (64.5 km), the gangs hold about seven toll points, mostly between Ganthier, Croix-des-Bouquets and the capital, charging $1,150 per 30-foot container, $576 per 20-foot container and $50 to $300 per small vehicle. Near the border (Malpasse to Fond-Parisien) community self-defense groups are still present. Trade crosses with Haitian carriers who have deals with the gangs.
feed.evidence: No source named; table photo
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.who: Radio Métronome (@Radio_Metronome), Haitian radio, citing Arcahaie Mayor René Wilner
feed.text: The mayor asks for air support, "including helicopters and kamikaze drones," so the police can fight back. Since about 2:45 a.m. on 31 Oct the attackers are said to have retaken Bercy, Vignier and Sourigole and burned several houses; a partial toll is at least seven dead and several wounded. The attackers came mainly from Cabaret, with reinforcements from Kenscoff and the Cul-de-Sac plain; police were fighting them at Thoman near the town center, and Carriès is also threatened. The groups are said to be tied to Izo 5 Segond (part of Cabaret) and Jeff Gwo Lwa (Montrouis).
feed.evidence: Named mayor; no photos

feed.text: "Bukele seems to confirm his deployment of troops to Haiti is not a 'rescue' mission," posted over a screenshot. Dr. H. Salazar (17:05) reads Bukele's "Can confirm" under Trump's "They killed some of his people" the same way, and infers that the four technicians died two weeks ago.
feed.evidence: Analyst's reading of Bukele's posts; screenshot
feed.other: Another source says: no Salvadoran deaths have been announced, and Diario El Mundo says the troops are still searching.

feed.where: X, statement in English and Creole
feed.text: The force answers reports of explosive devices and aerial bombardment by security forces in Haiti, including claims about helicopters: "The GSF does not use explosive devices in its operations. This includes the Salvadoran contingent and aircraft operating under the GSF, which do not carry explosive devices." It says it follows its rules of engagement and international human rights law, and that "any suggestion to the contrary is without foundation." The statement places the Salvadoran contingent and its aircraft under the force.
feed.evidence: Official written statement from the force; no media
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.who: Rezo Nodwes (@rezo_nodwes), Haitian news site, press review
feed.text: A press review of 30 and 31 Oct: Salvadoran soldiers patrolled Tabarre and Clercine on Friday in trucks and armored vehicles near the airport, and local media say they set up a base in Tabarre near the US Embassy (EFE, via Diario El Mundo). La Prensa Gráfica says Bukele will keep adding troops until the four are recovered. Infobae, citing El Tiempo, says a Colombian C-130H (FAC 1005) carried Salvadoran troops and equipment from San Salvador. "No rescue is announced." Rezo Nodwes notes that EFE did not say whose helicopters flew over the Friday patrols. AP (via Africanews) also shows a heavily armed convoy with new armored vehicles in Tabarre on Friday.
feed.evidence: Review of named outlets; AP photo of the convoy

feed.text: Bukele quote-posted the White House clip of Trump's Mar-a-Lago remarks ("They killed some of his people") with two words: "Can confirm." He did not say what he was confirming. Rolfy Martínez (04:13) reads it as Bukele confirming that gangs killed his people, but says it still cannot be said whether the four are dead and that he awaits formal word.
feed.evidence: Post by the president himself; no further detail
feed.other: Another source says: Drop Site notes that no Salvadorans have been reported killed and that Bukele has said burned bodies found last week were not theirs.

feed.text: Infos Partege reports celebrations in Arcahaie as gang members' corpses are dragged through the streets by motorcycles. It says loyal police officers working with the local self-defense brigade drove the gangs back. A brigade member is quoted: "We always feel like we get mixed signals from the government in the capital. Tonight we ignored them and took care of our business... We can do this ourselves if they would get out of our way!"
feed.evidence: Video, about 11 seconds; brigade member not named
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.who: White House Rapid Response (@RapidResponse47), clip of President Trump
feed.text: Asked about Bukele, Trump said: "I did speak to him. He said that he has a big problem with Haiti... They killed some of his people. I said, 'You're running your country. You have to do what you have to do.'" Drop Site says he spoke to reporters at his Halloween party. This is the first time Trump himself has spoken of the call that Axios reported on 30 Oct.
feed.evidence: Video of the president speaking
feed.other: Drop Site adds that no Salvadorans have been reported killed. Corvington Matin (French) adds that the Haitian government still says nothing to the public about the Salvadoran forces.

feed.who: Descargador Miniaturas News (Carlos Ramírez), citing Haitian outlet Amerique.info7; shared by Rolfy Martínez
feed.text: At least 12 civilians were killed and seven gang members wounded in a revenge attack on Bèssi and nearby places in Arcahaie on 31 Oct, after the killing of "Galaxie," according to Amerique.info7. The piece says other outlets reported fires, gunfire and people fleeing but gave no death count.
feed.evidence: Figures from Amerique.info7's unnamed sources (Amerique.info7 not opened by us)
feed.other: Another source says: Le Concret Info and Vant Bèf Info report deaths and burned houses but give no count.

Three minutes earlier HaitiInfoProj said gangs were massing to attack "for Bawon Laplen" (Lanmò San Jou) and that only the Arcahaie brigade, police and local authorities were holding them off, with "bullet ridden corpses" around the town. It also shared a Creole appeal for a missing man, Jack Louis, lost in the flight.
feed.evidence: Text credited to "IP"; earlier post describes images; Rolfy Martínez posted three photos

feed.text: Economist Etzer Émile announced he is running for president. Nancy Roc says his campaign is funded by businessman Patrick Moussignac (no evidence given).
feed.evidence: News headline; Nancy Roc's claim has no source

feed.text: Drop Site sets Bukele's denial against the record: five Salvadoran helicopters landed in the Dominican Republic on 28 Oct (Diario Libre); at least 78 Salvadorans had served in the Gang Suppression Force since early 2025; the UNA-Haiti letter cited no death toll or specific incidents. But it notes that after the 18 Oct ambush the force and police ran a helicopter-backed offensive in the Cul-de-Sac plain, and that the government's drone task force with Vectus has struck around the capital; Human Rights Watch counted at least 1,243 killed by its strikes from March 2025 to January 2026.
feed.evidence: Written summary citing Diario Libre and Human Rights Watch

feed.who: Magazine Haïti (@maghaiti), citing Arcahaie acting agent Wilner René
feed.text: From dawn on Saturday 31 Oct armed men attacked Vigner, Thoman and Sou Rigòl in Arcahaie and people fled; Wilner René asks the police and the Task Force to act quickly. It recalls that "Galaxie" and others were killed on 29 Oct at Bercy by drone strikes of the police and the Task Force.

feed.who: @kapulet (Luis Cab), Dominican account, relaying Lanmò San Jou
feed.text: In a new video, the 400 Mawozo leader Lanmò San Jou says his grave is ready and that Bukele is coming for him and is close, in Croix-des-Bouquets. The poster notes he first denied the ambush, then asked for peace, and now says he will die.
feed.evidence: Video, about 52 seconds, of the gang leader; place not shown

feed.text: A Haitian man complains on video that El Salvador will "privatize" Haiti, and criticizes Haitians who cheer foreign troops instead of equipping their own army and police to fight the gangs.
feed.evidence: Video, about two minutes; man not named

feed.text: "The battle is still on": after a short lull, gunfire resumed in Arcahaie; police and the brigade members reinforcing them have begun to push the gangs back.
feed.evidence: Text only; no source named

feed.text: Bukele answers UNA-Haiti's charge of air strikes on civilians: "Bombs? Our mission doesn't even have bombs at its disposal… Our attack helicopters didn't arrive in Haiti until October 29," and "they haven't flown a single mission." He calls the NGOs "lobbying firms for criminals and cartels." EFE (San Salvador, 1 Nov) says the letter is dated 28 Oct, a day before the helicopters came. Corvington Matin quotes him as calling it "a lie, pure and simple."
feed.evidence: Post by the president with a photo of the letter
feed.other: Another source says: Drop Site earlier reported the letter as dated 29 Oct; EFE and Gunther Eagleman say 28 Oct. Listín Diario saw helicopters armed at Jimaní on 29 Oct before flying to Haiti.

feed.who: TVGT Noticias (@TVGTNoticias), Guatemala, citing La Capital News
feed.text: Residents of Canaan took to the streets to denounce the gangs and point out where they operate, in the same commune where the four Salvadorans were ambushed.

feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: Gang members march in the street singing "Nap boule la" ("We are going to burn it") and call for burning everything, after gang members in the area began to fall.
feed.evidence: Video, about 38 seconds; place and date not shown

feed.text: El Salvador now has about 2,400 to 2,800 troops in Haiti searching for the four; there is still no real information on where they are, whether they are held, or whether they are alive.
feed.evidence: Video, about 96 seconds; no source given for the figure

feed.who: Le Quotidien 509 (@lequotidien509), Brigitte Benshow and newsroom
feed.text: A long dossier on what is known after 13 days. Points: El Salvador's decree 679 (in force 2 Oct) lets troops operate from the Dominican Republic, renews itself automatically, keeps the troops under Salvadoran jurisdiction and bars handing any soldier to an international court or a foreign state; the first night El Día reported five Salvadorans taken, later four, never explained; a police source says the men left their vehicle at a market at Santo 15-17; the force told the paper it does not give figures or deployment plans. It notes the UN Panel of Experts traced ammunition marked "ERD" (Dominican Army) to 400 Mawozo, and that some Vectus contractors are Salvadoran according to a Crisis Group analyst, but "no document links Prince to the Salvadoran operation."
feed.evidence: Documents cited (decree, communiqués, UN reports); one unnamed police source

feed.text: Lanmò San Jou shows a batch of new long guns and says he is ready to fight. Parrain Infos asks whether they came from the Dominican Republic.
feed.evidence: Video, about 44 seconds; origin of weapons not shown

feed.text: Phénil Gordon Désir, lawyer and head of the party "Ayiti 2054," was transferred to the United States on Saturday 31 Oct, three days after Interpol and the judicial police arrested him in Pétion-Ville in the Jovenel Moïse murder case.
feed.evidence: Text with one photo; no official statement cited
feed.other: Another source says: Corvington Matin, citing "our contact," says he was extradited on Friday 30 Oct.

feed.text: Gang members post video counting cash "they will pay Bukele," money Rolfy Martínez says they extorted from Haitians, while the Salvadoran army, police and the Gang Suppression Force hunt them.
feed.evidence: Video, about 30 seconds, filmed by gang members

feed.who: Parrain Infos (@ParrainInfos), citing journalist Guerrier Henry
feed.text: Six members of 400 Mawozo turned themselves in at the Clercine police station "to escape death."
feed.evidence: Named journalist as source; no media
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.evidence: Two photos; no source named
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

The mayor asks the Task Force to step in. Vant Bèf Info later blamed the "Taliban" gang and reported dead, wounded and burned houses; Le Concret Info says the mayor reported houses and vehicles set on fire. feed.evidence: Station's own statement; no detail
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.text: The Cabaret gang leader known as "Galaxie" and about ten of his men were killed by kamikaze drone strikes on Thursday 29 Oct in an operation by the Haitian police and the Task Force at Bercy, between Cabaret and Arcahaie. The mayor said on Radio Télé Caraïbes's "Gran Boulva" news that other gang members fled, causing tension in nearby places including Lévêque. Le Nouvelliste (30 Oct), citing a local source, also says the police, "backed by the Task Force," killed several gang members including Galaxie. Radiographie says at least ten were killed and that police armored vehicles pushing into Lévêque emptied the Cabaret market.

feed.who: Rolfy Martínez (@RolfyMartinez), relaying Lanmò San Jou of 400 Mawozo
feed.text: A video from Lanmò San Jou mocks Bukele's prisons. It was viewed more than 100,000 times within hours.
feed.evidence: Video from the gang leader himself; place and date not shown

It says graduates go straight to communities "to dislodge criminal gang networks, hold cleared territory" alongside special police units, the Haitian army and the Gang Suppression Force, and that candidates are screened for gang ties with "retinal scan lie detection technology."
feed.evidence: Official statement
feed.other: The statement does not mention El Salvador.

feed.other: Another source says: other outlets credit the police with the Task Force (Le Nouvelliste, Magazine Haïti) or with the Arcahaie brigade (HaitiInfoProj).

feed.evidence: Reporter's post; experts quoted in the article (we could not open the article; the New York Times blocked our reader)

feed.who: Carel Pèdre (@carelpedre), Haitian radio and TV host
feed.text: In Creole: "In a game like this there's 9 million dollars in bounties out there on the gang leaders' heads!"
feed.evidence: No source given for the figure

feed.text: The 37th police class, named "Dessalines," graduated: 1,189 new officers, 242 of them women, the third group of the P-4000 program. feed.text: Mirambeau says more than 1,000 Salvadoran soldiers landed "without any legal framework," and that five armed forces now operate in Haiti: the police, the army, the Gang Suppression Force, Erik Prince's task force and Bukele's army, with "no coordination between them." He adds: "Yes, we are tired. And we all want Bukele's army to pour bullets on the bandits so we can catch our breath," but warns that past foreign forces brought cholera and abuse.

feed.who: US Embassy in Haiti (@USEmbassyHaiti), quoting the State Department's Western Hemisphere bureau (@WHAAsstSecty)
feed.text: The US thanked Germany for airlifting more than 600 tonnes of priority equipment from Bangladesh for the Gang Suppression Force.
feed.evidence: Official post

feed.who: Corvington Matin (@Corvington_CM) and Vant Bèf Info (@vantbefinfo)
feed.text: Canada said on 30 Oct that people under international sanctions for violence, corruption or ties to armed gangs should not take part in the coming elections; Corvington quotes it as saying those who fund gangs "have no place in these elections." Corvington says, citing its own information, that Canada's ambassador has been firm with Prime Minister Fils-Aimé for two weeks.
feed.evidence: Canadian government statement; Corvington's sources not named

feed.who: Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), Center for Economic and Policy Research
feed.text: Johnston reports another cargo flight from El Salvador to Haiti today and says the flights carrying personnel do not show on public flight trackers. feed.evidence: Analyst's post; he cites flight tracking
links: CEPR, "Haiti Doesn't Need War. It Needs Peace." (Mar 2026)

feed.text: The judicial police (DCPJ) issued a call for Phénil Gordon Désir in the investigation of the 2021 killing of President Jovenel Moïse. He was seen in Pétion-Ville on 28 Oct; Le Quotidien 509 also describes it as a search, not an arrest.

feed.text: Corvington says more than 2,500 Salvadoran soldiers are deployed with combat helicopters and armored vehicles, and that Colombia helped carry troops and equipment.

feed.text: The government and the UN Development Programme are preparing to retake and rebuild downtown Port-au-Prince under a project called AVANSE. The police and the Haitian army are securing and clearing the Champ-de-Mars; work is to start in November, with operations around Parliament from January 2027.

feed.who: Marc Caputo, Axios, relayed by Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston)
feed.text: Axios reports that Bukele called Trump on Tuesday to make sure Washington would not object to the surge, and Trump told him, "Do what you have to do," warning that "it might get messy." Up to 2,000 troops are going in and the number "could double or triple"; Haiti approved a bilateral agreement on Wednesday; the force works alongside the Gang Suppression Force and Erik Prince's Vectus Global. Axios says Haiti "may be a test case" for Bukele and Prince "to act as public-private proxies for U.S. muscle." One source says Rubio wants Haiti "off the radar"; another says US requests for drones and transport planes were officially turned down and that Colombia may serve as an unofficial go-between. Rep. Brian Mast: "I hope the mission is revenge, retribution and destruction of the gangs."
feed.evidence: Sources briefed on the call, not named; Mast named
feed.other: The Haitian Times relays the report and adds that the terms of the bilateral agreement have not been made public.

feed.text: UNA-Haiti, a diaspora group (not part of the UN), wrote to Secretary-General Guterres on 29 Oct that Salvadoran forces have hit civilian areas of Croix-des-Bouquets, Canaan and the Cul-de-Sac plain since 22 Oct with air strikes, helicopter gunships and heavy weapons: "Children are being killed not by gangs, but by foreign bombs." It says families are "hiding under beds" and asks for a halt and a UN investigation.

feed.text: Seven military helicopters stopped on 29 Oct at the 14th Infantry Battalion heliport in Jimaní, 53 km from Port-au-Prince: five Salvadoran MD500Es (numbers 48, 49, 52, 53 and 54) at about 3 p.m. and two Black Hawks at 4:10 p.m. Dominican troops refueled and checked them and their weapons were fitted; all seven left for Haiti at 5 p.m. Diario Libre says the MD500Es were flown from San Salvador to Santo Domingo in a National Airlines Boeing 747-400, and Foreign Minister Bisonó says the Dominican Republic helps with transit, equipment, medical evacuations and blood but sends no troops into combat.

Otherwise: "if they don't hand them over the easy way, we will rescue them the hard way, and along the way we will finish them off." He said the four were medical evacuation technicians and "not a valid military target," and that El Salvador has no interest in Haiti's resources.

feed.where: Miami Herald, Port-au-Prince and San Salvador
feed.text: Bukele addressed Haitians in a video message: "This is not an operation against the Haitian people." The Herald reports that at least one airlift was flown by a US military aircraft, that Colombia helped with logistics, that more than a dozen flights have landed, and that no signed agreement with Haiti has been made public.

feed.where: Miami Herald, Port-au-Prince and the lower Artibonite
feed.text: The Salvadoran contingent has grown from a 125-member aviation unit to at least 2,000 troops (special forces, marines, infantry and support) and was expected to reach about 2,500 by the end of Thursday, against 2,526 for the whole Gang Suppression Force before the surge. Most of the Salvadorans have not had the force's two-week human rights course, and sources say no status-of-forces agreement has been signed. The Herald counts five security structures now at work: the Haitian police, the Haitian army, the Gang Suppression Force, a drone task force using contractors linked to Erik Prince, and the Salvadorans. The troops stay at a camp near the US Embassy. Former defense minister Jean Dorneval: "They need to have a legal framework or else they are mercenaries." Vanda Felbab-Brown of Brookings warns about the rules of engagement and the civilian toll of drone strikes. In the lower Artibonite, Bertide Horace welcomes Bukele while Gran Grif has pressed an offensive on Petite Rivière since 19 Oct, with bodies in the river and armed men in the town center. Jean Gilles Bernard Camille says a Salvadoran helicopter was nearly shot down. Doctors Without Borders has suspended its mobile clinics.
feed.evidence: Named people quoted; several sources not named
feed.other: Not yet reported by others: the near shootdown of a helicopter and the lack of human rights training.

feed.who: Reuters (via The Straits Times and CBC)
feed.text: About 1,000 Salvadoran soldiers have deployed to Haiti, says a security official in Haiti who asked not to be named. It is unclear who commands them or how long they will stay. A US military official says Southern Command C-130s helped move them; flight-tracking shows the flights, and a lawmaker from Bukele's party posted a photo of soldiers on a plane. The Gang Suppression Force has about 2,000 personnel, a third of its planned strength; before the ambush there were at least 124 Salvadorans. Pierre Espérance (RNDDH, a Haitian rights group) welcomed the troops but warned: "Not everybody living in gang-controlled areas are gangsters." Wilson Joseph of 400 Mawozo denies holding the men. Analyst Luis Contreras expects some troops to work outside the force's chain of command, coordinating with Erik Prince's company.
feed.evidence: Anonymous security official and unnamed US military official; named analyst and rights advocate; flight-tracking data
feed.other: El Español (Spain) adds that direct flights by the Ecuadorian airline Aeroregional carried troops; Radio Télé Galaxie and other Haitian outlets relayed the 1,000 figure in French and Creole.

feed.text: Flights carrying Salvadoran soldiers and equipment kept landing on Monday: at least a dozen since Thursday, at least two on Sunday, a chartered cargo flight Monday afternoon and a second expected that evening. El Salvador has not said how many it has sent, but the number had reached 450 by Saturday "with hundreds more expected." On Monday Salvadoran forces under the GSF banner and Haitian police ran a joint operation in the Bon Repos area. "Bukele is reportedly seeking to deploy more troops to bolster the force and to operate independently of the mission, answering directly to his commander on the ground in Haiti." Sources told the paper that 400 Mawozo backed up Chen Mechan's gunmen in the 18 Oct attack. Lanmò San Jou also says he holds three Haitian police officers and showed a video of them criticizing the government for caring more about the Salvadorans than about them.

feed.who: Presidency of the Dominican Republic, on President Luis Abinader's weekly press program (LA Semanal, Monday 26 Oct)
feed.text: Abinader: "We will act in coordination with the government of Haiti, but we will not allow those gangs within 20 kilometers of the border." He says the border is at its highest level of protection and the Dominican Republic is not at its moment of greatest risk. Defense Minister Lt. Gen. Carlos Antonio Fernández Onofre says the gangs control at least 70 percent of Port-au-Prince, people are moving mainly west rather than toward the border, at least two Haitian self-defense groups stand between the nearest gangs and the border, and intelligence shows no organized gangs in the north near Ouanaminthe (Juana Méndez). Foreign Minister Víctor "Ito" Bisonó says the Dominican Republic does not take part directly in operations, as a neighbor, but gives the GSF logistics: transit for contingents, medical evacuations, air permits, blood shipments and moving military cargo. It says about 2,181 international personnel are deployed, with a goal of about 5,500 within three months.
feed.evidence: on the record, named officials; official release

"The gangs are holding civilians in these areas to use them as human shields."

feed.text: Seventeen days after the UN Panel of Experts report, the Dominican government has still not explained how Dominican Army (ERD) ammunition made in 2022 reached Haitian gangs. The report says "most" of about 900,000 rounds diverted from Dominican police stocks in 2024 went to 400 Mawozo and other groups in Port-au-Prince. The Defense Ministry says no transfer was authorized; Foreign Minister Ito Bisonó says the rounds date from the Trujillo era, but the report also cites rounds the Dominican authorities said they bought in 2022 from a maker in Colombia. A companion story (13:04) puts the value of the diverted police ammunition at over 92 million pesos and names the officers charged in Operation Pandora.
feed.evidence: UN Panel of Experts report, named officials
links: Listín Diario, value of the ammunition

feed.who: Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic, speaking to reporters in Santiago; reported by Diario Libre
feed.text: Says the Dominican Republic has sent two more battalions, heavy equipment and artillery to the southern border, on top of about 11,000 men already deployed, and that he will meet the defense and foreign ministers and speak to Bukele again on Monday. feed.other: Another source says: EFE puts the force at more than 1,000 soldiers.

feed.text: Reports the Gang Suppression Force received badly burned remains on Saturday afternoon, wrapped in several layers of garbage bags, from HERO, a relief group contacted "through humanitarian channels." A HERO worker: "We hope this brings some closure, but we are in no way claiming it is them." The remains were to go for forensic testing. Says El Salvador had 450 special forces in Haiti as of Friday, and that the force had made no statement.
feed.evidence: named reporter; an unnamed HERO employee quoted
feed.other: Bukele (02:12, before this story) says the remains are not his men. Radio Télé Galaxie (Haiti) calls the group "Hero Client Rescue, funded by the United States," citing the New York Times.

feed.other: Bukele says the remains are not his men. Johnston deleted his own first post on it: "Times story has been updated and Bukele denying."
